Published: 43 seconds ago Myanmar Zarla Distribution Co.,Ltd. takes innovation honour at Asian Innovation Excellence Awards 2026 The company combined physical distribution, digital commerce, data, and fulfilment to create a connected operating model for Myanmar’s retail market.
Myanmar Zarla Distribution Co.,Ltd. received an accolade in the Myanmar Business Model Innovation of the Year - Business Services category at the Asian Innovation Excellence Awards 2026 for ZARLA Connected Commerce, which integrated its distribution operations with digital ordering and business services for traditional retailers.
Myanmar’s traditional trade market remains heavily dependent on relationships between shop owners and field sales representatives. Retailers may need to wait for scheduled visits to place orders, learn about promotions, or receive updated product information. ZARLA developed a hybrid model that retained these existing relationships whilst giving retailers another channel for accessing its distribution network.
BAHOZAY, its B2B commerce platform, allows shop owners to browse products, check promotions and product information, and submit orders without relying solely on sales visits. These transactions connect to the distributor’s existing warehousing, inventory, sales, and delivery operations rather than operating as a separate e-commerce system.
The platform also works alongside SAP ERP, ZARLA’s Distribution Management System, field-sales monitoring, and data analytics. This structure connects digital customer activity with the same operational systems used to manage physical distribution and fulfilment.
Field sales representatives remain part of the model. They support retailer onboarding and explain how to use the platform, whilst customer-engagement teams assist with continued adoption. BAHOZAY therefore supplements physical visits instead of replacing the salesforce, giving shop owners more flexibility over when they interact with the distributor.
The business has also used the connected ecosystem to extend services beyond ordering. Collaboration with CB Bank and Mastercard introduced a pathway for eligible shop owners to access financing linked to their purchasing activities. ZARLA has also identified payments, loyalty programmes, insurance, promotional tools, surveys, advertising, and brand engagement as potential services within the same digital relationship.
Data from platform activity provides further visibility into customer demand and operational constraints. Increased digital ordering, for example, highlighted the relationship between product availability, stock allocation, and the ability to fulfil orders placed through the platform.
ZARLA Connected Commerce consequently brings customer engagement, ordering, distribution, fulfilment, data, and business services into one operating structure built around Myanmar’s traditional retail sector.
The Asian Innovation Excellence Awards honours companies that achieve measurable outcomes and address key challenges through innovation and operational improvement, recognising initiatives that drive meaningful progress across diverse industries in the region.
